Semantic memory

Semantic memory as a network of concepts

Linked concepts let a memory support questions that were not specified when its information was stored.

M. Ross Quillian

AI topics

Explore related entries. Larger tags appear on more entries.

MemoryRecallSemantic networksKnowledge representation

The contribution

Quillian represented knowledge in a connected network and described a program that searched those relations to identify meanings and draw inferences. The model treated recall as an active use of structured knowledge, making stored information useful beyond a fixed list of prewritten questions and answers.

What this does not establish

The report proposed and simulated selected semantic abilities. It did not show that a small hand-built network captured all human long-term memory.

Why this date?

1966 dates the original report. SHRDLU uses a 1966 citation label while naming the later chapter in Semantic Information Processing. The report and chapter are distinct publication versions.

This entry follows the linked publication. Read the source and date conventions.
